knowledge:
- key_parameters:
    - alleleFreq: Numeric value specifying the population minor allele frequency (MAF) of the rare variant to calculate exact sharing probabilities.
    - kinshipCoeff: Numeric value representing the mean kinship coefficient among pedigree founders to correct for relatedness.
    - carriers: Character or numeric vector specifying the subset of pedigree members assumed to carry the rare variant.
    - useAffected: Logical; if TRUE, restricts the sharing probability calculations to affected pedigree members.
    - nSim: Integer specifying the number of Monte Carlo simulations to run for estimating sharing probabilities under non-standard founder assumptions.
    - founderDist: A custom function defining the distribution of the variant among founders for Monte Carlo simulations.
    - filter: Character string (e.g., 'bonferroni') specifying the multiple testing correction method based on potential p-values in multipleVariantPValue.
    - alpha: Numeric significance level used for multiple testing filtering.
    - splitPed: Logical; if TRUE, automatically generates all carrier subsets and their sharing probabilities within RVsharing.
    - pattern.prob.list: A list of vectors containing precomputed sharing probabilities for all possible carrier subsets in each family.
    - nequiv.list: A list of vectors indicating the number of equivalent subsets for each sharing probability.
    - N.list: A list of vectors containing the number of carriers in each subset.
    - type: Character string (e.g., "count") specifying the test type in RVgene.
- alternatives:
    - kinship2: Used for plotting and managing pedigree structures.
    - snpStats: Used for reading LINKAGE pedigree files and representing genotype data as SnpMatrix objects.
    - VariantAnnotation: Used for reading VCF files and converting genotypes to SnpMatrix objects.
- when_to_use: Use this package when analyzing rare genetic variants in multiplex families with a dichotomous phenotype (e.g., disease status) to test for linkage and association, especially when sample sizes are small or variants are extremely rare.
- pitfalls:
    - Assuming founders are unrelated when they are actually related, which can inflate false positive rates (corrected using kinshipCoeff or Monte Carlo simulations).
    - High computational cost for enrichmentPValue when the true p-value is extremely small (mitigated by setting a minimum p-value threshold).
    - RVgene currently does not accept a pedigreeList object; it requires a plain list of pedigree objects.
    - Incompatible carrier subsets (e.g., a descendant carrying a variant but not an affected ancestor through whom it must have passed) must be manually removed from the subset list for partial sharing tests.

workflows.name: single_or_multiple_variant_sharing
workflows.intent: Compute sharing probabilities and p-values for single or multiple rare variants across one or more pedigrees.
workflows.stages:
1. Load pedigree structures and genotype data.
2. Calculate sharing probabilities for individual families or multiple families using RVsharing.
3. Compute p-values for single variants across families using multipleFamilyPValue.
4. Compute p-values for multiple variants across families using multipleVariantPValue, optionally applying Bonferroni correction based on potential p-values.
5. Perform sensitivity analysis for minor allele frequency (MAF) and kinship coefficients.
6. Run an enrichment test across all variants using enrichmentPValue.
workflows.code:
data(samplePedigrees)

# store the pedigrees
fam_type_A <- samplePedigrees$firstCousinPair
fam_type_B <- samplePedigrees$secondCousinPair
fam_type_C <- samplePedigrees$firstCousinTriple
fam_type_D <- samplePedigrees$secondCousinTriple

# re-label the family ids for this example
fam_type_A$famid <- rep('SF_A', length(fam_type_A$id))
fam_type_B$famid <- rep('SF_B', length(fam_type_B$id))
fam_type_C$famid <- rep('SF_C', length(fam_type_C$id))
fam_type_D$famid <- rep('SF_D', length(fam_type_D$id))

p <- RVsharing(fam_type_D)

# compute the sharing probabilities for all families
fams <- list(fam_type_A, fam_type_B, fam_type_C, fam_type_D)
sharing_probs <- suppressMessages(RVsharing(fams))
signif(sharing_probs, 3)

# compute p-value for this sharing pattern
sharing_pattern <- c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE)
names(sharing_pattern) <- names(sharing_probs)
multipleFamilyPValue(sharing_probs, sharing_pattern)

pedfile <- system.file("extdata/sample.ped.gz", package="RVS")
sample <- snpStats::read.pedfile(pedfile, snps=paste('variant', LETTERS[1:20], sep='_'))

A_fams <- lapply(1:3, function(i) samplePedigrees$firstCousinPair)
B_fams <- lapply(1:3, function(i) samplePedigrees$secondCousinPair)
C_fams <- lapply(1:3, function(i) samplePedigrees$firstCousinTriple)
D_fams <- lapply(1:3, function(i) samplePedigrees$secondCousinTriple)
fams <- c(A_fams, B_fams, C_fams, D_fams)
famids <- unique(sample$fam$pedigree)
for (i in 1:12)
{
    fams[[i]]$famid <- rep(famids[i], length(fams[[i]]$id))
}
sharingProbs <- suppressMessages(RVsharing(fams))
signif(sharingProbs, 3)

result <- multipleVariantPValue(sample$genotypes, sample$fam, sharingProbs)
result <- multipleVariantPValue(sample$genotypes, sample$fam, sharingProbs, filter='bonferroni', alpha=0.05)

# calculate p-values for each MAF
freq <- seq(0,0.05,0.005)
variants <- names(sort(result$pvalues))[1:3]
pvals <- matrix(nrow=length(freq), ncol=length(variants))
pvals[1,] = sort(result$pvalues)[1:3]
for (i in 2:length(freq))
{
    sharingProbs <- suppressMessages(RVsharing(fams, alleleFreq=freq[i]))
    pvals[i,] <- multipleVariantPValue(sample$genotypes[,variants], sample$fam, sharingProbs)$pvalues
}

# calculate p-values for each kinship coefficient
kin_coef <- seq(0, 0.05, length=6)
variants <- names(sort(result$pvalues))[1:3]
pvals <- matrix(nrow=length(kin_coef), ncol=length(variants))
pvals[1,] = sort(result$pvalues)[1:3]
for (i in 2:length(kin_coef))
{
    sharingProbs <- suppressMessages(RVsharing(fams, kinshipCoeff=kin_coef[i]))
    pvals[i,] <- multipleVariantPValue(sample$genotypes[,variants], sample$fam, sharingProbs)$pvalues
}

enrichmentPValue(sample$genotypes, sample$fam, sharingProbs, 0.001)

workflows.name: gene_based_partial_sharing
workflows.intent: Perform joint analysis of multiple rare variants within a gene, allowing for partial sharing among affected relatives.
workflows.stages:
1. Precompute sharing probabilities, carrier subset sizes, and equivalent subset counts for all possible carrier configurations in each family using RVsharing.
2. Load VCF files and convert them to SnpMatrix objects using VariantAnnotation::genotypeToSnpMatrix.
3. Align SnpMatrix objects and pedigree objects into named lists.
4. Run the gene-based joint analysis using RVgene to obtain exact p-values allowing for partial sharing.
workflows.code:
fam15157.pattern.prob = c(RVsharing(samplePedigrees$secondCousinTriple,carriers=c(15,16,17)),
    RVsharing(samplePedigrees$secondCousinTriple,carriers=c(15,16)),
    RVsharing(samplePedigrees$secondCousinTriple,carriers=c(15)))
fam15157.N = 3:1
fam15157.nequiv = c(1,3,3)

fam28003.pattern.prob = c(RVsharing(samplePedigrees$firstAndSecondCousinsTriple,carriers=c(36,104,110)),
RVsharing(samplePedigrees$firstAndSecondCousinsTriple,carriers=c(36,104)),
RVsharing(samplePedigrees$firstAndSecondCousinsTriple,carriers=c(104,110)),
RVsharing(samplePedigrees$firstAndSecondCousinsTriple,carriers=c(36)),
RVsharing(samplePedigrees$firstAndSecondCousinsTriple,carriers=c(104)))
fam28003.N = c(3,2,2,1,1)
fam28003.nequiv = c(1,2,1,1,2)

ex.pattern.prob.list = list("15157"=fam15157.pattern.prob,"28003"=fam28003.pattern.prob)
ex.nequiv.list = list("15157"=fam15157.nequiv,"28003"=fam28003.nequiv)
ex.N.list = list("15157"=fam15157.N,"28003"=fam28003.N)

data(famVCF)
fam15157.snp = VariantAnnotation::genotypeToSnpMatrix(fam15157.vcf)
fam28003.snp = VariantAnnotation::genotypeToSnpMatrix(fam28003.vcf)

ex.SnpMatrix.list = list(fam15157=fam15157.snp$genotypes,fam28003=fam28003.snp$genotypes)
ex.ped.obj = list(fam15157=samplePedigrees$secondCousinTriple,fam28003=samplePedigrees$firstAndSecondCousinsTriple)

sites = c(92,119)

RVgene(ex.SnpMatrix.list,ex.ped.obj,sites,pattern.prob.list=ex.pattern.prob.list,nequiv.list=ex.nequiv.list,N.list=ex.N.list,type="count")
